flags: StealthGas's 40,551 cbm vessel Eco Wizard was damaged by an explosion in a Russian port in July 2025 and has been unable to be employed since July 2025.

StealthGas resolved the insurance claim for the loss of one of its vessels, increasing cash and cash equivalents and short term investments from $168.3 million as of June 30, 2026 to over $250 million as of the September 2, 2026 earnings release.

Following the March 2026 outbreak of war in the Middle East and the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz, StealthGas's vessel Eco Oracle remained in the Persian Gulf and was unable to exit as of the annual report.

business_model.basis: Stated in the 20-F Item 4 business overview (P1) and Item 5 overview (P3).
business_model.claim: StealthGas owns and operates a fleet of LPG carriers providing international seaborne transportation for liquefied petroleum gas products including propane, butane, butadiene, isopropane, propylene, vinyl chloride monomer, and ammonia, occasionally chartering in additional vessels.
quotes: We own a fleet of LPG carriers providing international seaborne transportation services to LPG producers and users.

Our LPG carriers carry various petroleum gas products in liquefied form, including propane, butane, butadiene, isopropane, propylene and vinyl chloride monomer, which are all byproducts of the production of crude oil and natural gas.
On occasions we charter-in vessels to supplement our own fleet and employ them both on time charters and voyage charters.

business_model.basis: Stated in 20-F Item 4 fleet disclosures (P1) and November 2026 Form 6-K filings (P5, P6).
business_model.claim: As of year-end 2025, StealthGas operated 29 LPG carriers (including a JV vessel), which stood at 28 LPG carriers (339,134 cbm total capacity) as of April 2026, before agreeing in November 2026 to acquire the Eco Merlin, Eco Enchanted, Eco Texiana, and Eco Nebula for Mar-Sep 2027 delivery subject to stockholder approval.
quotes: As of December 31, 2025, we had a fleet of 29 LPG carriers, including one JV vessel.
As of April 1, 2026, our fleet is composed of 28 LPG carriers, including one JV vessel, with a total capacity of approximately 339,134 cbm.

The Special Meeting has been called by the Board of Directors of StealthGas Inc. for the stockholders to approve the Vessel Acquisition, as defined and described in the following Notice of Special Meeting of Stockholders and accompanying Proxy Statement.

business_model.claim: StealthGas charters its vessels to national, major, and independent energy companies, energy traders, and industrial LPG users, with customer concentration such that individual customers exceeded 10% of total revenues and its largest customers accounted for 34.1% of revenues in 2025 and 32.3% in 2024.
quotes: Principal charterers include producers of LPG products, such as national, major and other independent energy companies and energy traders, and industrial users of those products.
For the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, we had two customers and two customers, respectively, that accounted for more than 10% of our total revenues.
For the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, our three largest customers accounted for 34.1% and 32.3%, respectively, of our revenues.

business_model.basis: Stated in 20-F Item 4 Chartering of the Fleet (P1).
business_model.claim: StealthGas deploys its vessels globally without geographic restrictions, operating significantly in Europe and the Mediterranean as well as the Middle East, Far East, Africa, and the US Gulf.
quotes: While a significant part our fleet is operating in Europe and the Mediterranean, we deploy vessels globally and are not restricted to specific locations.
Some of the areas where we usually operate are the Middle East, Far East, Africa and the US Gulf.

business_model.basis: Stated in 20-F Item 5 Overview and Basis of Presentation (P3).
business_model.claim: StealthGas earns revenue by employing its carriers on fixed-rate period time charters (which may provide for rate adjustments and profit sharing) and spot/voyage charters priced for specific cargoes, having not used bareboat charters since mid-2022.
quotes: Under a time charter, the charterer pays a fixed rate per day over the term of the charter; a time charter, including a short term time charter, may provide for rate adjustments and profit sharing.
Under a voyage charter, we agree to transport a specified cargo from a loading port to a discharging port for a fixed amount.
We have not employed any vessels under bareboat charter since the middle of 2022.

business_model.basis: Stated in 20-F Item 5 (P3) and Q2 2026 earnings release Form 6-K (P7).
business_model.claim: As of September 2026, about 60% of StealthGas's fleet days for the remainder of 2026 were secured on period charters, with total fleet employment days across all periods generating about $90 million in contracted revenues excluding its JV vessel, up from 49% remaining-2026 coverage as of April 2026.
quotes: About 60% of fleet days for the remainder of 2026 are secured on period charters, with total fleet employment days for all periods generating about $90 million (excl. our single JV vessel) in contracted revenues.
As of April 1, 2026 and excluding our JV Vessel, 49% of our anticipated fleet days were covered by period charter contracts for the remainder of 2026 and 17% for 2027.

business_model.basis: Stated in 20-F Consolidated Statements of Income (F2) and Q2 2026 earnings release Form 6-K (P7).
business_model.claim: Consolidated revenues grew from $ 143,527,769 in 2023 to $ 167,262,185 in 2024 and $ 173,161,478 in 2025, while revenues for the June 2026 quarter were $42.9 million compared with $47.2 million in the prior-year quarter as average owned vessels declined from 28.3 to 26.4.
quotes: Revenues for the three months ended June 30, 2026, amounted to $42.9 million compared to revenues of $47.2 million for the three months ended June 30, 2025, based on an average of 26.4 vessels and 28.3 vessels owned by the Company, respectively.
The decrease in revenue is attributable to the decreased number of vessels.

business_model.basis: Stated in 20-F Item 5 (P3) and Q2 2026 earnings release Form 6-K (P7).
business_model.claim: Voyage revenues are driven by fleet size, voyage days, daily charter rates (averaging a daily TCE of $15,709 in the June 2026 quarter), and fleet operational utilization, which declined from 96.6% in 2023 and 95.4% in 2024 to 91.8% in 2025 as spot market days rose to 1,385.
quotes: Our voyage revenues are driven primarily by the number and size of the vessels in our fleet, the number of voyage days during which our vessels generate revenues and the amount of daily charter hire that our vessels earn under charters which, in turn, are affected by a number of factors, including our decisions relating to vessel acquisitions and disposals, the amount of time that we spend positioning our vessels, the amount of time that our vessels spend in dry dock undergoing repairs, maintenance and upgrade work, the age, condition and specifications of our vessels and the levels of supply and demand in the LPG carrier charter markets.
TCE rates improved for the larger vessels but were slightly reduced for the smaller vessels due to idle time, representing an average daily TCE of $15,709.

business_model.basis: Stated in 20-F Item 3.D Risk Factors (P2) and Item 5 (P3).
business_model.claim: LPG carrier demand and charter rates are cyclical and seasonal—typically stronger in fall and winter heating months—and are moved by global oil and petrochemical demand, newbuilding deliveries versus scrapping, trade tariffs, and shipping disruptions including the 2026 Middle East conflict that prevented the Eco Oracle from exiting the Persian Gulf.
quotes: The LPG carrier market is typically stronger in the fall and winter months in anticipation of increased consumption of propane and butane for heating during the winter months.
As of the date of this annual report, one of our vessels, the Eco Oracle, remains in the Persian Gulf and has not been able to exit due to the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

A significant decline in demand for the seaborne transport of LPG or a significant increase in the supply of LPG carrier capacity without a corresponding growth in LPG carrier demand could cause a significant decline in prevailing charter rates, which could materially adversely affect our financial condition and operating results and cash flow.

business_model.claim: Charter structure determines cost allocation: StealthGas pays vessel operating costs and commissions under time charters while the charterer pays voyage expenses, whereas StealthGas bears both vessel operating expenses and voyage expenses under spot/voyage charters.
quotes: Under a time charter, we are responsible for the vessel’s operating costs (crew, provisions, stores, lubricants, insurance, maintenance and repairs) incurred during the term of the charter, while the charterer pays voyage expenses (port, canal and fuel costs) that are unique to each particular voyage.
Under a voyage or spot charter, we are responsible for both the vessel operating expenses and the voyage expenses incurred in performing the charter.

business_model.basis: Stated in 20-F Consolidated Statements of Income (F2).
business_model.claim: In 2025, total operating expenses were 118,028,529 (table in USD), led by vessels' operating expenses of 52,980,264 (plus 933,616 related party), depreciation of 25,252,476, voyage expenses of 20,433,872 (plus 2,097,322 related party), general and administrative expenses of 8,333,449, related-party management fees of 4,445,120, and dry-docking costs of 3,602,010.

business_model.basis: Stated in 20-F Item 5 (P3) and Q2 2026 earnings release Form 6-K (P7).
business_model.claim: Voyage expenses are driven by spot market days, port and canal charges, EU ETS carbon allowances, commissions, and bunker fuel (36.9% of 2025 voyage expenses, lifting June 2026 quarter voyage expenses to $7.2 million from $4.4 million a year earlier), while vessel operating expenses are driven by crew wages, insurance, repairs, stores, and U.S. dollar exchange rates.
quotes: Voyage expenses include port and canal charges, bunker (fuel oil) expenses, carbon allowances under the EU ETS scheme and commissions.

Bunkers (fuel oil), the price of which has been relatively stable in the last few years but increased sharply in March 2026 as a result of the war in the Middle East between the U.S. and Israel and Iran, accounted for 36.9% of total voyage expenses for the year ended December 31, 2025, 33.2% of total voyage expenses for the year ended December 31, 2024, and 35.7% of total voyage expenses for the year ended December 31, 2023.
The $2.8 million increase in voyage expenses was mainly due to an increase in bunkers costs driven by an increase in the number of spot market days for the fleet and higher bunker prices.

Vessel operating expenses include crew wages and related costs, the cost of insurance, expenses for repairs and maintenance, the cost of spares and consumable stores, tonnage taxes and other miscellaneous expenses.

business_model.basis: Stated in 20-F Item 4 Commercial and Technical Management of Our Fleet (P1) and Item 5 (P3).
business_model.claim: StealthGas outsources technical, commercial, and administrative management to related-party Stealth Maritime for a fixed fee of $440 per vessel per day under voyage or time charters ($280 where third-party managers provide part of the services; $125 on bareboat), plus 1.25% of gross freight, demurrage, and charter hire, 1.0% on vessel purchases or sales, and cash executive compensation reimbursements ($1.0 million in 2025).
quotes: We have a management agreement with Stealth Maritime, pursuant to which Stealth Maritime provides us with technical, administrative, commercial and certain other services.
We are also obligated to pay Stealth Maritime a fee equal to 1.25% of the gross freight, demurrage and charter hire collected from the employment of our vessels.
Stealth Maritime will also earn a fee equal to 1.0% of the contract price of any vessel bought or sold by them on our behalf.
During the year ended December 31, 2025, such cash compensation was in the aggregate amount of $1.0 million.

business_model.basis: Stated in 20-F Item 5 Depreciation and Dry docking (P3).
business_model.claim: Depreciation is charged straight-line over 30 years from shipyard delivery down to a $350 per light weight ton scrap value, while dry-docking and survey costs are expensed as incurred ($3.6 million in 2025 and $5.3 million in 2024), creating period-to-period cost volatility.
quotes: We depreciate our vessels on a straight-line basis over their estimated useful lives, determined to be 30 years from the date of their initial delivery from the shipyard in the case of our LPG carriers.
Residual values used in depreciation calculations are based on $350 per light weight ton.
We expense costs associated with dry dockings and special and intermediate surveys as incurred which may affect the volatility of our results.

quotes: Our investments in joint ventures are accounted for using the equity method of accounting since we have joint control over the joint venture entities.

quotes: The capacity of the world shipping fleet appears likely to increase in the near term, although growth in the 3,000 to 11,000 cbm segment of small LPG carriers, the segment in which we have the largest operating presence, as well as the Handysize segment of LPG carriers in which we also operate, are expected to be limited in the period 2026-2027, as the order book is relatively small, while scrapping activity is stable.

quotes: We believe that we have established a reputation as a safe, cost-efficient operator of modern and well-maintained LPG carriers.

We also believe that these attributes, together with our strategic focus on meeting our customers’ chartering needs, has contributed to our ability to attract leading charterers as our customers and to our success in obtaining charter renewals.

competitive_position.claim: StealthGas depends on affiliated fleet manager Stealth Maritime to operate its business and holds a right of first refusal on Stealth Maritime's future LPG carrier acquisitions, though Stealth Maritime may manage competing third-party vessels.
quotes: We depend on our manager, Stealth Maritime Corporation S.A., to operate our business.

In addition, as long as Stealth Maritime (or an entity with respect to which Harry N. Vafias is an executive officer, director or the principal shareholder) is our fleet manager or Harry N. Vafias is an executive officer or director of the Company, Stealth Maritime has granted us a right of first refusal to acquire any LPG carrier which Stealth Maritime may acquire in the future.

This right of first refusal does not prohibit Stealth Maritime from managing vessels owned by unaffiliated third parties in competition with us, nor does it cover other sectors of the shipping industry, including product carriers or crude oil tankers.

competitive_position.claim: A considerable number of MGC vessels on order for delivery in 2026 and beyond could create vessel oversupply and reduce charter rates, vessel values, and profitability.
quotes: Beginning this year, 2026, and beyond there is a considerable number of vessels in the MGC segment on order scheduled for delivery that could lead to an oversupply of vessels.
An over-supply of ships may lead to a reduction in charter rates, vessel values and profitability.

competitive_position.claim: With vessels deployed in the spot market and 15 vessels scheduled to complete existing time charters during 2026, StealthGas faces lower earnings if expiring charters cannot be renewed on favorable terms.
quotes: As of April 1, 2026, of our 27 operating LPG carriers, including one JV Vessel and excluding two vessels we have agreed to sell, three were deployed in the spot market while another 15 were scheduled to complete their existing time charters during 2026.

If charter rates decline, our earnings may decrease, particularly with respect to our vessels deployed in the spot market, or those vessels whose charters will be subject to renewal during 2026, as they may not be extended or renewed on favorable terms when compared to the terms of the expiring charters.

competitive_position.claim: StealthGas depends on a small group of customers for a large share of revenue, with its largest customers generating 34.1% of revenues in 2025 and 32.3% in 2024, and individual customers exceeding 10% of total revenues in both years.
quotes: For the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, we had two customers and two customers, respectively, that accounted for more than 10% of our total revenues.
For the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024, our three largest customers accounted for 34.1% and 32.3%, respectively, of our revenues.
The loss of one or more of these customers could adversely affect our financial performance.

competitive_position.claim: The war in the Middle East between Iran and the U.S. and Israel and the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz in March 2026 disrupted Persian Gulf shipping, raised concerns over constrained LPG supply, pushed bunker prices sharply higher, and kept the Eco Oracle trapped in the Persian Gulf.
quotes: In March 2026, the outbreak of war in the Middle East between Iran and the U.S. and Israel, including strikes by Iran on energy infrastructure in a number of other Middle Eastern countries and related disruption of shipping in the Persian Gulf and the substantial closure of the Strait of Hormuz, has resulted in a sharp increase in oil prices and concerns that the supply of LPG may be significantly constrained for some period of time.
As of the date of this annual report, one of our vessels, the Eco Oracle, remains in the Persian Gulf and has not been able to exit due to the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz.

Bunkers (fuel oil), the price of which has been relatively stable in the last few years but increased sharply in March 2026 as a result of the war in the Middle East between the U.S. and Israel and Iran, accounted for 36.9% of total voyage expenses for the year ended December 31, 2025, 33.2% of total voyage expenses for the year ended December 31, 2024, and 35.7% of total voyage expenses for the year ended December 31, 2023.

competitive_position.claim: Geopolitical conflicts and maritime security risks threaten vessel availability and trading routes, illustrated by the Eco Wizard being unable to be employed since an explosion in a Russian port in July 2025, Houthi attack risks in the Red Sea and Suez Canal, and EU sanctions banning Russian-origin LPG.
quotes: For instance, our vessel, the Eco Wizard, was damaged by an explosion while in a Russian port in July 2025, and since that time has been unable to be employed as a result of the damage sustained.
The Company may take ships through the Suez Canal, and there is a high risk that Houthis might attack our vessels.
The sanctions, imposed by the European Union, include a ban on Russian-origin LPG, including LPG imported via Russia.

competitive_position.claim: Escalating U.S. tariffs imposed in 2025 and February 2026, retaliatory tariffs by China, and proposed U.S. and Chinese port fees create trade-war uncertainty that could reduce global LPG seaborne demand.
quotes: Tensions over trade and other matters remain high between the U.S. and China, which is the world’s largest importer of LPG and covers over half of its import needs from U.S. based producers.

A ruling by the U.S. Supreme Court in February 2026 invalidated many of the tariffs imposed by the U.S. administration in 2025, however, the U.S. administration immediately imposed new tariffs based on different statutory authority.
Although we do not have any Chinese-built vessels in our current fleet, it is unknown the effect that these new port fees will have on us, or our industry generally.

competitive_position.claim: Increased spot market deployment exposes StealthGas to voyage costs, driving voyage expenses up from $4.4 million in the second quarter of 2025 to $7.2 million in the second quarter of 2026.
quotes: Voyage expenses and vessels’ operating expenses for the three months ended June 30, 2026 were $7.2 million and $12.8 million, respectively, compared to $4.4 million and $12.8 million, respectively, for the three months ended June 30, 2025.
The $2.8 million increase in voyage expenses was mainly due to an increase in bunkers costs driven by an increase in the number of spot market days for the fleet and higher bunker prices.

competitive_position.claim: Longer-term competitive threats include regional economic or industrial slowdowns, LNG pipelines supplanting residential LPG, stricter environmental regulations, and technological innovation reducing charter income and vessel values.
quotes: Technological innovation could reduce our charter hire income and the value of our vessels.
We are subject to regulation and liability under environmental laws that could require significant expenditures and affect our financial condition and results of operations.

In particular, an adverse change in economic conditions affecting China, Japan, India, Southeast Asia or Europe generally could have a negative effect on the demand for LPG products, thereby adversely affecting our business, financial position and results of operations, as well as our future prospects.
increases in pipelines for LNG, in residential areas currently consuming LPG for cooking and heating, thus supplanting LPG for these particular residential uses.
